name: access_control_patterns
description: Missing access control on privileged/critical functions
question: The source file in `source` defines a function that performs a privileged or critical operation (e.g., withdrawing/transferring funds, minting tokens, changing ownership or roles, pausing/unpausing, upgrading, or setting sensitive parameters) as an external or public function, and that function has no access-control restriction whatsoever: no onlyOwner, onlyRole, restricted, or AccessManaged modifier, and no explicit msg.sender authorization check, so that any arbitrary caller can invoke it and directly compromise funds, ownership, or protocol configuration.
criteria: External/public function moves or withdraws Ether/tokens without any onlyOwner/onlyRole/restricted modifier or msg.sender check
External/public function mints tokens, changes fees, or updates critical parameters with no access-control guard
External/public function grants/revokes roles or transfers ownership without requiring caller authorization
External/public pause/unpause or upgrade function callable by any address, missing onlyRole/onlyOwner/restricted
Function is clearly intended to be privileged (name, comments, or state it mutates) yet omits any authorization check
No AccessControl/Ownable/AccessManaged inheritance or modifier is applied to functions performing sensitive state changes
